summary: No code was changed: the root cause was not found within the time budget, so no PR is opened. The stun bar is driven by BotHealthBar.UpdateStun (Assets/Scripts/Combat/UI/BotHealthBar.cs) polling the nearest GameEntity's stunDamage into HealthBarUI each LateUpdate, and the bar's maximum is fixed once in Setup from stunBufferSize. Static checks found the wiring identical on every variant: BotUISpawner exists only in the base Junkdog.prefab and JungleDog.prefab and no variant overrides it; the ancestor chain BotUISpawner > RibCage (PhysicsBoneLookAt) > PhysicsRig > root has no intermediate GameEntity; no variant overrides stunBuffer; and the only override shared by Spiked, Armored and Turbo Junkdog that Bloodhound lacks is CreatureID.difficulty. So the difference only appears at runtime. A diagnostic Play session never reached the combat scene: the editor was on an untitled scene, and an import-triggered recompile blocked the retry from Main Loader.
instructions:
Bug: for certain singleplayer enemies, the on-screen stun bar UI does not visually update/fill as the enemy takes hits, even though the enemy's actual stun accumulation is working correctly (they do eventually become stunned after enough hits). This affects:

1. All Junkdog enemy variants EXCEPT the base Junkdog and the Bloodhound Junkdog (those two work correctly).
2. All Jungledog enemy variants EXCEPT the normal/base Jungledog (that one works correctly).

Since the base variants of each enemy type display the stun bar correctly but the other variants in the same family do not, the issue is likely specific to how those variant enemy classes/prefabs/configs are set up relative to the base ones (e.g. missing or misconfigured stun bar component reference, overridden health/stun handling script, different prefab not wired to the UI update, or a variant-specific script that doesn't call the stun bar update logic that the base class uses).

Please investigate why the stun bar visual fails to update for these specific enemy variants while working for their base counterparts, and fix it so that the stun bar correctly reflects stun accumulation in real time for every affected Junkdog and Jungledog variant. Verify the fix in singleplayer by hitting each affected enemy type enough times to confirm the stun bar now visibly fills and that the enemy still becomes stunned at the correct threshold, and confirm the previously-working base Junkdog, Bloodhound Junkdog, and base Jungledog still behave correctly (no regression).
